title: The Laws of Shabbat #10 - "When the Fridge Light is On..." (1)

chapters.title: Introduction to the Fridge Light Issue
chapters.about: Defining the problem of a fridge light remaining on during Shabbat.

chapters.title: Understanding Mechabeh
chapters.about: Analyzing the prohibition of extinguishing and its application to modern lights.

chapters.title: Melacha She'eina Tziricha Legufa
chapters.about: Discussing the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Hachamim regarding intent.

chapters.title: Extinguishing Metal vs. Wood
chapters.about: Examining the Gemara's distinction between types of fires and their status.

chapters.title: The Tur and Shulchan Aruch
chapters.about: Reviewing historical halakhic sources on extinguishing fires in public areas.

chapters.title: The Double D'Rabbanan Approach
chapters.about: Explaining Rabbi Ovadia Yosef's leniency using a double rabbinic prohibition.

chapters.title: Trapping Flies and Closing Chests
chapters.about: Using the laws of trapping as a parallel for closing a fridge door.

chapters.title: Summary of the Halakhic Strategy
chapters.about: Concluding the current approach for handling the fridge light.

summary: Rabbi Harari explores the halakhic considerations surrounding a refrigerator light that remains on during Shabbat. He examines the concepts of Mechabeh, Melacha She'eina Tziricha Legufa, and Psik Resheh, specifically focusing on the approach of Rabbi Ovadia Yosef regarding the use of a double D'Rabbanan to address the situation. The class serves as the first part of a broader discussion on these laws.
questions: What should I do if I open my fridge on Shabbat and the light is on?
Is it permitted to close a fridge door if it will certainly turn off the light?
How does the concept of a double D'Rabbanan apply to Shabbat laws?
Why is extinguishing a light in a modern refrigerator considered a rabbinic prohibition?
What is the difference between a direct action and a roundabout action on Shabbat?
